As of 300 AM Thursday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Record heat will continue through Friday. 

An anomalously strong sub-tropical ridge centered in 00Z/15th upr 
air data over the TN Valley, with standardized 500 mb height 
anomalies ~2 sigma, will progress ewd and off the South Atlantic 
coast through 12Z Fri. On the nrn periphery of that ridge, series of 
MCVs from dissipated or weakening convection from the DelMarVa to 
nrn Middle TN will progress generally ewd and across the srn Middle 
Atlantic today.  Deep layer flow will then strengthen and back to 
swly ahead of an intense, positively-tilted, full latitude, and 
increasingly-phased trough --one comprised of a srn stream cyclone 
now over CO and a vigorous nrn stream shortwave trough over MB-- 
forecast to stretch from wrn QC to the lwr MS Valley by 00Z Sat. 

At the surface, an outflow boundary/wind shift across the Virginias 
and lwr OH Valley, related to the aforementioned dissipated or 
weakening convection there, will drift ssewd and probably across the 
nrn Piedmont and nrn Coastal Plain of NC by late this morning-
midday. A synoptic front lags the outflow and was analyzed at 07Z 
from n-cntl DE through nrn VA and cntl WV. While this boundary will 
also move generally swd and in backdoor fashion across VA this 
morning, it will likely not move into the ne Piedmont and nrn 
Coastal Plain of NC until later this afternoon and evening, where it 
will briefly stall. The front will then retreat nwd later tonight 
and Fri, as mass response strengthens ahead of the intense trough 
aloft and a related surface cyclone forecast to deepen considerably 
while tracking across the Great Lakes and Northeast on Fri. 

Temperatures today will be generally persistence ones equatorward of 
the approaching synoptic front, which will offer cooling throughout 
VA and only into the far ne Piedmont and nrn Coastal Plain of NC. 

While heights throughout the column will fall ahead of the 
approaching trough aloft on Fri, related cooling will be limited 
over cntl NC until late in the day and more-so Fri night. As such, 
temperatures on Fri will again be near persistence ones, to perhaps 
a couple of degrees lower than previous days' warm sector ones. A 
gusty swly surface wind may take a little edge off the heat while 
also boosting the temperature at RDU to, or within a degree of, the 
latest 90 degree day and probably the third consecutive in this 
stretch, provided the backdoor front holds north of RDU as expected 
today.  


KEY MESSAGE 2... A strong cold front will sweep across central NC 
Friday evening, with a significant cooldown for the weekend. There 
is still some potential for patchy frost, but forecast uncertainty 
has increased.

Aloft, a potent nrn stream s/w will drop into the upper MS Valley 
and track sewd across the Great Lakes Thu and Fri, deepening the 
trough over the ern US as it interacts with another s/w ejecting 
enewd from the cntl Rockies to the Great Lakes Thu/Thu night. The 
positively tilted trough will continue to amplify as it moves ewd 
across the eastern US and offshore over the weekend. Model spread 
has increased from Sat onward, with some more recent guidance 
showing a low developing within the trough over the Carolinas 
Sat/Sat night, possibly lingering over the region for awhile, 
slowing the troughs ewd progression, while others develop a low 
offshore. At the surface, an area of low pressure lifting newd 
across the mid-MS and OH Valley on Thu will deepen as it continues 
across the Great Lakes and Northeast US Thu night/Fri. The trailing 
cold front will move across central NC late Fri evening into Fri 
night, currently progged to be moving into the nw Piedmont around 
00Z Sat. A ~1037 mb Canadian high centered over the s-cntl Plains on 
Sat will build into the region in the wake of the front as it tracks 
newd across the mid-MS and OH Valley regions on Sat. There is some 
uncertainty beyond Sat, with some models showing a coastal low 
developing as along the front as it moves offshore, while others 
show a more progressive front continue ewd over the Atlantic. The 
latter solution would allow the high to settle over the mid-
Atlantic, while the former would take the high enewd across the nrn 
mid-Atlantic/Northeast US on Sun. 

The varying solutions noted above will impact numerous weather 
parameters (temps, winds, precip, etc.), resulting in a low-
confidence forecast Sat night onward.  

The chance for rain continues to increase, as does the duration, 
coverage, and uncertainty. Forecast amounts are still somewhat 
light, with generally a quarter of an inch or less expected Fri 
night through Sat night. The low-level jet is expected to strengthen 
over the area Fri eve, with 25-35 kts at 925mb. The pressure 
gradient will also be quite strong as a ~1037 mb high builds ewd. 
Expect gusty winds with and behind the front Fri eve through Sat. 

Temperatures should fall about 25-30 degrees from Friday aft to Sat 
morning. By Saturd
